result:
Mornings have a way of arriving quietly. Before the street wakes fully, the light lies thin across rooftops, catching on windows and turning ordinary glass into something almost theatrical. A bicycle leans against a gate. Somewhere, a kettle begins its small metallic song. These details rarely make the news, but they give the day its first shape.

I like walking without a destination and allowing attention to wander. A newly planted tree may seem impossibly ambitious, reaching toward a sky it has never known. A shopkeeper sweeps fallen petals into careful piles. Pigeons circle above the square as if discussing urgent matters. The world does not need interpretation to be mysterious; sometimes mystery is simply what remains when we stop trying to explain it.

My pockets usually contain a notebook, a pen, and a spare button. The button serves no obvious purpose, but I refuse to discard it. Perhaps some day it will mend a coat, decorate a paper planet, or become the treasure at the bottom of an imaginary chest. This possibility is enough.

Ordinary things reward patience. Books open to pressed flowers. Old maps show coastlines that no longer exist. Cups leave faint rings on tables, temporary circles connecting one moment to another. Even dust, examined closely, becomes a landscape of glitter and shadow.

Perhaps happiness is less like finding a hidden door than noticing the handle. It waits in bread, in a friend’s joke, in the click of a lock closing behind you as you return home.
